facts.fact: Diploma/graduate (e.g. BTech) pass-outs register as a 'General student' on the NATS 2.0 portal (nats.education.gov.in)
facts.quote: Students who have completed Diploma or Graduate level education from recognized institutions can register on the portal as General students

facts.fact: NATS is implemented by the Boards of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT), autonomous bodies under the Ministry of Education's Department of Higher Education
facts.quote: is an Autonomous body under the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Govt. of India. BOAT (SR) has been implementing the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS)

facts.fact: Students still pursuing their diploma/degree use the Sandwich/AEDP route instead
facts.quote: Note: If you are still pursuing diploma/ graduate, opt for Sandwich/ AEDP.

facts.fact: Training is on-the-job training lasting 6 months to 1 year
facts.quote: a practical, hands-on On-the-Job-Training (OJT) based skilling opportunities with duration ranging from 6 months to 1 year.

facts.fact: At the end of training the apprentice gets a Certificate of Proficiency from the Government of India
facts.quote: At the end of the training period the apprentices are issued a Certificate of Proficiency by Government of India which can be registered at all employment exchanges across India as valid employment experience.

facts.fact: There is no guarantee of a job after the apprenticeship
facts.quote: There is no guarantee of employment after completion of training as an apprentice.

facts.fact: The candidate should ideally have no previous work experience
facts.quote: The student should not ideally have any Previous work experience to be eligible for registration & apprenticeship training.

facts.fact: The minimum monthly stipend for graduate/degree apprentices is Rs 12,300
facts.quote: Graduate apprentices or degree apprentices or degree in any stream Rs. 12,300 per month.

facts.fact: The revised rates come from the Apprenticeship (Amendment) Rules, 2025, notification G.S.R. 610(E) dated 3 September 2025, in force from 11 September 2025
facts.quote: Please find enclosed a copy of the Gazette Notification (No. G.S.R.61O(E), dated 3rd September 2025) issued by this Ministry regarding amendments to the Apprenticeship Rules, 1992. The Rules comes in force effective from the date of publication of the Gazette notification ie. 11-09-2025.

facts.fact: The earlier graduate stipend under NATS was Rs 9,000 a month (diploma Rs 8,000)
facts.quote: The apprentices who have completed graduate and diploma programme in Engineering, Humanities, Science and Commerce will be given stipend of Rs.9,000/- and Rs.8,000/- per monthrespectively.

facts.fact: BOAT (WR) circular of 13.05.2026 says the revised minimum stipend rates are implemented under NATS, for the Government share of stipend, with effect from 01.04.2026
facts.quote: the minimum prescribed stipend rates under The Apprenticeship Rules, 1992, stand revised and will now be implemented under the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) for the Government share of stipend, with effect from 01/04/2026.
facts.note: BOAT WR/2026/529 dated 13/05/2026, read by OCR of the scanned PDF; its table gives graduate Rs 9,000 -> Rs 12,300 and vocational Rs 7,000 -> Rs 9,600 per month.

facts.fact: The minimum monthly stipend for Technician (diploma) apprentices is Rs 10,900
facts.quote: Technician apprentices or diploma holder in any stream or sandwich Rs. 10,900 per month

facts.fact: The minimum monthly stipend for Technician (vocational) apprentices is Rs 9,600
facts.quote: Technician (vocational) apprentice or Vocational Certificate holder or Rs. 9,600 per month

facts.fact: These are minimum rates; an establishment may pay more
facts.quote: The above rates represent the minimum total stipend payable to apprentices. Establishments are encouraged to pay stipends more than the minimum prescribed rates.
facts.note: Read by OCR of the scanned BOAT(WR) circular of 13.05.2026.

facts.fact: The stipend is paid by the establishment, and 50% of it is borne by the Government of India
facts.quote: During the period of apprenticeship, the apprentices are paid a stipend amount, 50% of which is reimbursable to the employer from Government of India.

facts.fact: The Government share is paid by Direct Benefit Transfer to the apprentice's bank account
facts.quote: Note: The Government share of monthly stipend, if any, shall be paid by the Government through Direct Benefit Transfer to the apprentice‘s bank account

facts.fact: To receive the DBT, the apprentice's bank account must be Aadhaar-seeded and mapped in the NPCI mapper
facts.quote: Step 3: Ensuring the active bank is AADHAAR SEEDED & MAPPED IN NPCI MAPPER.

facts.fact: Registration includes Aadhaar e-KYC with UIDAI
facts.quote: As part of the student registration process, the portal integrates e-KYC with UIDAI to authenticate the student’s Aadhaar number and verify their identity.

facts.fact: An example in the old answer: a BOAT(SR) notification offers Rs 10,000/12,300-type rates for its own seats
facts.note: The only BOAT(SR) own-seat notice found (nats.education.gov.in/uploads/events/sr/BOAT_Notification_for_engagement_of_Apprentices.pdf, applications 07.03.2025-17.03.2025) offers Rs 10,000 (graduate) and Rs 8,000 (diploma), set before the Sept 2025 revision and below today's Rs 12,300 minimum, so it is no longer an example of paying more; no BOAT(SR) notice offering Rs 12,300 for its own seats was found on nats.education.gov.in (BOAT SR page) or by search. Remove the example.

facts.fact: Step 1: open nats.education.gov.in and click the 'Student' button at the top right
facts.quote: On the home page, click on the Student button located on right top.

facts.fact: Step 2: choose the 'General student' tab (for Diploma/Graduate pass-outs) and click 'Student Registration'
facts.quote: Step 2: Select the General student tab having the prompt (For Diploma/ Graduate pass-out students) Note: If you are still pursuing diploma/ graduate, opt for Sandwich/ AEDP. Refer to that particular manual available on the footer of the NATS 2.0 home page. Step 3: Click on the Student Registration tab.

facts.fact: Step 3: keep ready a personal email, mobile number, Aadhaar for e-KYC, the degree/provisional certificate as a PDF under 1 MB, and an APAAR ID
facts.quote: Aadhaar number for e-KYC. 4. Qualifying Degree/ Provisional certificate in PDF format, and size less than 1 MB. 5. APAAR ID.

facts.fact: Without an APAAR ID, create one on the ABC portal first
facts.quote: If student doesn't have an APAAR ID, create one from ABC portal click here: Create APAAR ID .

facts.fact: Step 4: verify the mobile number and email by OTP
facts.quote: Step 5: Provide Mobile number & Email for OTP verification.

facts.fact: Step 5: complete Aadhaar e-KYC with the OTP sent to the Aadhaar-linked mobile
facts.quote: Enter the OTP received on aadhaar linked mobile number and click verify.

facts.fact: Step 6: fill the registration form (institute, course, specialisation), set a password and submit
facts.quote: Educational details which are to be selected from dropdown values like Institute name, its state & district. Which education background either graduate or diploma, the course & specialisation details. The password to profile should also be set before final submitting the registration.

facts.fact: Step 7: click the verification link sent by email to activate the account
facts.quote: Once the registration form is submitted, an email will be sent to the registered email with a verification link. The student has to mandatorily verify from the email to activate their account.

facts.fact: Step 8: log in and complete the profile; its last steps are training preferences (location and field) and 'Preview profile & final submit'
facts.quote: Step 4: Training preferences. Fill in the location & field preferences, if any. Step 5: Preview profile & final submit:

facts.fact: In educational details, fetch the certificate from DigiLocker using APAAR or upload it as a PDF
facts.quote: Where there is option to fetch the issued certificate from Digi locker using APAAR (or) Upload the certificate in PDF format.

facts.fact: Step 9: once the profile is complete, apply to establishments' apprenticeship openings on the portal
facts.quote: The student enrolment ID is generated, and now eligible to apply for apprenticeship opportunities, and obtain an apprenticeship training.

facts.fact: A contract offered by an establishment must be accepted within 15 days, or it is auto-rejected
facts.quote: What will happen if a contract is not accepted within 15days days ? Contract will be marked auto-rejected and candidate will no longer have the facility to re-accept it.

facts.fact: After the student accepts, the contract goes to BOAT for final approval
facts.quote: student has to accept the contract request from establishment firstly, in order to send request to BOAT for final confirmation.

behaviour: Gives the registration steps and the stipend from the NATS pages, the Apprenticeship (Amendment) Rules 2025 gazette and BOAT notices, with a citation (nats.education.gov.in); sends a BTech graduate to the NATS 2.0 portal as a General student; mentions Aadhaar e-KYC and APAAR; gives no promise of a placement. If the bot cannot read the scanned BOAT stipend notices, it says the stipend follows the minimum rates under the Apprentices Act and links the notice rather than stating Rs 9,000 as current.
fail_if: It says Rs 9,000 (pre-revision) or Rs 4,984 (old) is the current stipend; sends a BTech graduate to the MSDE NAPS/apprenticeshipindia portal as the main route; omits e-KYC/APAAR; promises a job; invents registration fees.
summary: All registration steps and the Rs 12,300/10,900/9,600 minimum stipends confirmed (GSR 610(E) gazette text, NATS manual/FAQ/about-us); w.e.f. 01.04.2026 is only in scanned BOAT notices (manual); the BOAT(SR) Rs 10,000/12,300 example is not supported and is removed.
